I've now been playing for 50 hours, which I think is enough for me to give a fairly accurate review of this game. It's not fun.

This game is a chore to play a lot of the time and there are many reasons for that, but there are also reasons as to why this game is really entertaining. 

Lets start with some of the main reasons that put me off of this game, firstly, not EVERY game needs a fishing mechanic, I promise you, adding fishing doesn't just make it a 10/10, it feels forced the more I see it in games that just don't need it. There are hundreds of tutorials to teach you very basic things, like how to speak to a certain NPC and what they do, cool just don't do that for every single NPC in the game. I don't need multiple different tutorials to know what smithing or melding is in this game, I feel like I can figure it out by looking at the menu. 

The next main point I know I'm going to get reamed for so if you reply to this review, please note: I do not care about your personal opinion as to why "I'm wrong" Monsters should not take 10-20 minutes to hunt. I should not be spending legitimately 18 minutes fighting a special version of one of the first monsters that has extra powers. That just makes it feel like a tedious chore that makes me sigh the more I chug along doing the same attacks to the enemy that just decides to spam roar, flying away, tremors, other stunning abilities and just generally getting in my way. Stuns in this game should not take 5-10 seconds before you regain control of your character. No matter how much I wiggle my left stick, or spam WASD, it doesn't feel like it changes any difference in how soon I regain control.

If you're playing this game for the first time and you're going in blind, with nobody telling you anything about the game, you're going to see that you have really useless "leather gear" with 2 defence per piece, or you'll have the "defender gear" which has 50 defence per piece. It's obvious as to what you're going to pick, why would you purposely select weaker gear over what's clearly better. Issue is, people like to call that defender gear, cheating armour. You won't ever need anything else until the DLC with that gear and even going through the base game with the defender gear, trying out other monster gear on the side, which just made me feel so annoyingly squishy it STILL takes 15-20 minutes per new monster to defeat, if you're lucky you can get them down in 5-10 minutes if you're clearly higher level than them and it's not your first rodeo.

There are however good factors about this game, don't get me wrong. The character customisation feels great, a cat companion is always fun, graphics look amazing (even if it's unoptimised). fairly entertaining range of weapons and skillsets, I personally really enjoy the insect glaive, took me a little while to understand how it works, and it's very fun to leap around monsters all day.

I still -at the end of the day- cannot recommend this game to anyone who's entering this series from here. I was gifted this game by a friend, I told him I'd play it but since I'm also a completionist, I'd need to 100% this game before I even think about a different Monster Hunter game. I'll be playing this game for another 400-500 hours before I see my blue ribbon on Steam. I just don't think this game is more entertaining than it is tedious. When I play a game, I expect to be having fun, not open a game into a really really long boring book with a story that is just uninteresting. I don't expect to play a game that is just hit one monster 203 times before it dies, (Not exaggerating, I actually did the maths on a specific monster, that is just boring and long.)

I'll still personally be playing this game until I reach 100% achievement completion and I will continue to complain about it to my friends because this game does anger me in many ways. Who knows, maybe the other Monster Hunter games are better than this, unfortunately, this is the only one I know. and I don't think it is that good, definitely not enough for me to recommend it to someone. I apologise if I anger you about my review, this isn't the case of me "getting good" it is purely just the design of the game not being good enough for me to enjoy.

I know the small amount of time I've put in the game will ring some alarm bells for the deep-seated fans of the franchise, so I'd like to preface that I'm staunch in my belief that first impressions matter and, thus, the first hour of gameplay is the most important in any game. 

That all said, my experience in Monster Hunter World has been quite a journey so far. I originally bought and refunded the game. I realise I was extremely strict with my initial playthrough and decided to give it another go when it went on sale.

The first hour experience is exactly that, an experience. The music is good, the voice acting (Japanese) is the usual unparalleled quality you'd expect, the introduction to the lore doesn't demand that much from the player and feels like a standalone story despite being set in a continuous universe being games. This is the best decision a studio can do as it allows players to settle into the world and give them a chance before they start to dig deep into the lore. Genshin Impact, Witcher 3, Bioshock and Borderlands all do this very well too.

The combat, the main draw of this franchise, startled me in my first attempt at this game. I loved that the game gave you all the time in the world to practice with whichever weapon you wanted without trying to shuffle you along to the next step. I love dual wielding, so I chose that, and I felt it was a passable experience in the training area. I was let down immensely once I put the skills to the test on moving enemies. In my current attempt at playing, I decided to not only spend more time in the training area, but to use a controller, and I realised the problem. This combat focused game is a TERRIBLE PC port. It feels like you can't really play this game without a controller.

Lastly, Astera is possibly one of the coolest hub settlements I've seen in any game I've played. Nothing is too far away, it's absolutely gorgeous and viewing it for the very first time after escaping the dinosaurs is breathtaking.

A solid 8/10.

A truly great game which stands up pretty well in 2026. Monster hunter world offers diverse weapon movesets, fun bosses, and a lot of interesting systems to interface with. Compared to perhaps soulslike or character action games, it can feel weird, clunky, or slow, but as a fan of those types of games, this is much the same, it just takes adjustment as it exists in an area apart from the both of those. If you like soulslike or character action games, you'll be a fan of Monster Hunter World.

There is unfortunately many nits to pick at in this game, though I still consider it very enjoyable.
- The handler is horrifically annoying
- The introduction sequence is a deluge of uninteresting and overwhelming tutorials. If you think you'll like this game, be prepared for almost an hour and a half of nonsense before you truly get cut loose.
- There are a number of features which I feel sort of bog down the game even if they sometimes offer interesting choices. The slinger for one is cool in concept but its rarely useful outside and scales horrifically into iceborne.
- The Zorah Magdaros fight is one of the worst quests in all of video games. An effectively unlosable autoscroller where any player with half a brain and navigational skills will end up standing there and waiting with nothing to do for no joke 10 minutes. Literally standing with nothing happening. I'm not exaggerating.
- Some monster hitboxes are inconsistent which hurts all players
- Some monster hitboxes aren't part of the same groups which hurts counter type weapons like the longsword since you can get hit by both boxes, nulling your counter.
- There is clearly exactly one gameplay meta and generally build choices are traps or nothingburgers.
- Decorations require an insane amount of grinding for good ones.
- The story, in my opinion, is dumb and uninspired. It has very weird colonization and destruction of native life vibes without very good justification. It's a game about killing monsters, yeah, but you're a team of monster researchers and ecologists? It's just weird. They could have done much better by focusing on the aspects of survival or that its a "Way of life" like ive been told they do in older games. There's no real threat against the characters for most of the game so they're just kind of going around killing monsters for no particularly good reason. Granted, you aren't here for the story. You're here to kill monsters.

There are also a lot of nits to pick at specifically with the DLC iceborne
- Unlike base game, you can get stuck where you've done all of the content and are still 50 master rank levels short of the next content which unlocks at level 100. This would take, no joke, 20 hours to grind up with no new content. I think this is a horrific design choice. I want to fight the next challenge when I beat the previous. I'll grind if I need new equipment, not arbitrary number going up.
- Some end game content has terrible game design. Alatreon is the most eggregious in my opinion, reqiuring very specific means to defeat him which you basically need to look up online as he sports an *actually* instakill move you need to weaken through specific actions that are not explained. He also seems to expect you to swap weapons or gamify when you break his horns. Swapping weapons is not possible without dying in that fight so you have to micromanage hornbreaks normally.
- Generally Iceborne ramps up the difficulty post credits which isn't the worst thing. End game content should be hard. However a lot of it is plainly rather frustrating. The game's design choice of "Pack as many potions as you like" lets the monsters have massive damage numbers which causes any hit to be grounds for the next potion or crafting potions in combat or farcastering back to get more potions. It's a ridiculous loop compared to other games. It would be more enjoyable if the bosses did less damage and I could only take one pouch of potions. This would let you get more playtime between the next mandatory potion while also making it a resource consumption choice.
- Clutch claw starts good, ends bad. At first I didn't get the hate for clutch claw. It seemed fine and an interesting gameplay choice. Unfortunately, endgame iceborne it is absolutely vital and required. You need those wallbangs. You need those tenderizes. It controls like a semi truck and has knock offs so inconsistent most end game guides just tell you to use temporal mantle so you literally can't get knocked off. A 40% damage buff is just not possible to ignore in endgame. It breaks up the flow of the fight and all around decreases the amount of time you spend doing what the game is good at. Using your weapon.
- Where this becomes obvious is Fatalis. You need every lick of damage you can get on that guy. You must use absolutely meta builds. There is basically no build diversity. Clutch claw is not optional. You need everything. Me and a friend timed out with 40% of his health remaining with all of these things. This is very frustrating from a game design perspective. There is no "Play your way" apart from your weapon style choice. This being said, Fatalis is an incredibly gratifying experience to beat and I think very well designed compared to some of the endgame monsters. The fight itself is fun, but at that point most of the remaining game is not. You'll all use the same gear and same weapons. There is no other way to win.

Though I critiqued it a lot, I still find MH world an excellent game. I just probably won't come back to it once hitting Rise or Wilds which refine its systems even further and enhance the VERY lacking quality of life that world has.

☀ weapons variety and how much different they feel from eachother, changing weapon feels like starting again from 0 like you started a new save file, but the more you play the faster you will learn different weapons and adapt quickier.
(my main weapon? ough... today GS? LS? CB? SA? maybe bow who knows i basically use everything)
☀ good italian VA 
☀ lovely exploration (i still get lost in the ancient forest HELP) and with some little cute secrets and sometimes breathtaking landscapes/
☀ incredible monsters design: velkhana, alatreon, fatalis, odoragon, kulve taroth, safii'jiva just to mention some of the best ones.
☀ amazing vibes, i'm really happy everytime i boot up the game
☀ interesting progression for being a rpg. it only relies on your equipment so the skill factor is more involved than usual and levels are just a thing to see how much time/experience a hunter has.
☀ AMAZING, GODLY music we are on dragon quest levels here.
☀ the best community i ever witnessed in gaming, from newbies like me to MR999 players with 2-3k hours in the game being super wholesome and always and available for helping, even for the most tedious things like crown hunting. (the mentality usually is "failed quest?, no problem let's try again).
☀  solid performance? besides in the guiding lands the game runs smooth even with reshade active.
☀  good fashion and in general weapons and armors design. not always more of that in the negative part...
☀  balanced difficulty overall, even if at the end it spikes like crazy, alatreon and fatalis being unlocked at mr24? really? maybe a veteran can take them down. but a newbie will never ever beat fatalis at mr24, i personally did it around MR100 with the help of some really lovely guys, now i'm working on slaying him solo! AT velkhana and Alatreon are already down (more on my yt channel)

[h1]What i disliked or found annoying[/h1]

☀ resuming the fashion topic, there are downsides too sadly. overall in base world most armor sets and weapons design are quite bland and honestly most of them look the same. i'm really grateful that iceborne and TA updates introduced and improved the overall fashion.
☀ the costant need to tenderize monster parts. i don't hate this mechanic on his own, but i find it annoying that you have to tenderize so many times during a hunt it becomes a chore. in MP it isn't that bad but when playing solo? nah.
☀ shitty servers, it happens way to often to be disconnected from a lobby or from a group in the middle of a hunt it's really annoying.
☀ decos farming maybe being too brutal? i got really lucky so i'm not complaining much, but i know people that in 500-600-700h only have 1 critical eye II jewel, that has to be very painful.
☀ horrible anti-aliasing as usual it makes the game super blurry, i can't it looks soo bad. i have to rely on reshade since i'm playing in 1080p and playing without AA isn't a option for me.
☀ questionable achievements choices i get that the 100% should makes you experience "everything" a game has to offer, but why then there are no achievements for taking down the hardest monsters in the game? no slay 10-50 arch tempered monsters? no slay fatalis? alatreon? no?

[h1]Quick conclusions[/h1]
summary, give a shot to mhw:i (especially now that is cheaper than ever) so much quality and quantity for such low price? no need to think twice. hop on and get slowly absorbed by this fantastic world, see you around hunters.

Oh my GOD why have I not played this sooner. I grinded all the IGH you see in the summer of 2025 and I was absolutely obsessed with this game. This is simply peak fantasy in my opinion; A giant, awe-inspiring world, towering monsters, and a protagonist ready to take on anything that stand in their way. Playing this game with friends and randoms was nothing but a blast. I was always looking forward to that next upgrade, that next armor set I unlock, that next monster / area I get to discover, and doing it a dozen more times for my own materials or helping out others.
This game has officially made me a fan of this series and gotten me excited about any new installments in the future. One of my favorite games of all time now and I can't wait for my next hunt in the next world I'll get to adventure through.
